headline: Every palindrome has one center
statement: Count all contiguous substrings of s that read the same forward and backward. Equal strings at different positions count separately.
intuition: A palindrome expands symmetrically around a character or a gap. There are n odd centers and n-1 even centers. Extend matching endpoints and count every successful expansion.
approach: Map each center to equal pointers for odd length or neighboring pointers for even length.
While endpoints are in bounds and equal, increment the count and expand outward.
correctness: Every palindromic substring has a unique center and radius. For that center, all its inner pairs match, so expansion reaches and counts it. Conversely, each successful expansion creates matching endpoints around a palindrome, so every counted substring is valid. Unique center/radius pairs prevent double counting positions.
bruteForce: Enumerate all O(n²) substrings and test each in O(n), for O(n³) time. Expansion reuses the inner palindrome property.

complexity.explanation: Repeated-character strings permit quadratic expansions; only pointers and a count are stored.

pitfalls: Repeated equal text at different positions counts repeatedly.
A single character is always a palindrome.
